title: Theft
old_text: Intending to take dishonestly any movable property out of possession of any person without consent, and moving that property.
new_text: Dishonestly taking movable property without consent, with a new proviso prescribing community service for first-time petty theft under Rs. 5,000 upon restitution.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 3 years, or fine, or both
punishment_new: Imprisonment up to 3 years, or fine, or both; first-time theft under Rs. 5,000 upon return of property: community service
explanation: BNS Section 303 consolidates IPC Section 378 (definition) and Section 379 (punishment). Significantly, it introduces community service as an alternative reformative penalty for first-time offenders who steal property valued under Rs. 5,000 upon restitution.

title: Snatching
old_text: No specific statutory definition in IPC; prosecuted under general theft (Section 379) or hurt/robbery provisions.
new_text: Theft is snatching if the offender suddenly, quickly, or forcibly seizes, grabs or takes away movable property from any person or possession.
punishment_old: None (prosecuted as theft: up to 3 years)
punishment_new: Imprisonment up to 3 years, and fine
explanation: BNS Section 304 introduces snatching as an independent codified criminal offence for the first time in Indian penal jurisprudence. It covers sudden, quick, or forcible grabbing of phones, chains, or bags, bridging the gap between simple theft and violent robbery.

title: Theft in dwelling house, or means of transportation or place of worship, etc.
old_text: Theft in any building, tent or vessel used as a human dwelling or for custody of property.
new_text: Theft in any building, tent, vessel, means of transport, or place of worship used as a dwelling or for custody of property.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 7 years, and fine
punishment_new: Imprisonment up to 7 years, and fine
explanation: BNS Section 305 replaces IPC Section 380, explicitly widening the scope to include theft inside any 'means of transport' (trains, buses, aircraft) and 'place of worship' alongside residential buildings, tents, and vessels.

title: Theft by clerk or servant of property in possession of master
old_text: Theft committed by a clerk or servant of property belonging to or in the possession of their master or employer.
new_text: Theft committed by any clerk, employee or servant of property in possession of master or employer.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 7 years, and fine
punishment_new: Imprisonment up to 7 years, and fine
explanation: BNS Section 306 corresponds directly to IPC Section 381 punishing aggravated theft committed in breach of domestic or workplace fiduciary trust. It carries rigorous imprisonment up to 7 years and fine.

title: Theft after preparation made for causing death, hurt or restraint in order to committing of theft
old_text: Theft having made preparation for causing death, hurt, or restraint, or fear thereof, in order to commit theft or escape.
new_text: Theft after making preparation for causing death, hurt, or restraint to commit theft or effect escape.
punishment_old: Rigorous imprisonment up to 10 years, and fine
punishment_new: Rigorous imprisonment up to 10 years, and fine
explanation: BNS Section 307 replaces IPC Section 382 penalizing theft accompanied by lethal or violent preparations. An offender carrying weapons or stun implements while committing theft incurs severe liability up to 10 years rigorous imprisonment.

title: Extortion
old_text: Defined in Section 383; punishments graded across Sections 384 to 389 depending on fear of death, grievous hurt, or accusation.
new_text: Consolidates extortion definition and sentencing tiers, punishing putting a person in fear of injury to dishonestly induce delivery of property.
punishment_old: Basic: up to 3 years; aggravated (fear of death/grievous hurt): up to 10 years or imprisonment for life
punishment_new: Basic: up to 7 years, or fine, or both; aggravated: up to 10 years or life imprisonment and fine
explanation: BNS Section 308 consolidates IPC Sections 383 through 389 into a unified extortion framework. The basic penalty for extortion has been elevated from 3 years to up to 7 years, while preserving higher sentencing tiers for threats of death or heinous accusations.

title: Robbery
old_text: Robbery defined in Section 390; punishments graded in Sections 392, 393 (attempt), and 394 (voluntarily causing hurt in robbery).
new_text: Consolidates robbery definition and punishments: theft or extortion converted into robbery by causing or attempting death, hurt, or wrongful restraint.
punishment_old: Rigorous imprisonment up to 10 years (highway: 14 years); voluntarily causing hurt: life or RI up to 10 years
punishment_new: Rigorous imprisonment up to 10 years and fine (highway sunset-to-sunrise: up to 14 years); causing hurt: up to life or 10 years
explanation: BNS Section 309 merges IPC Section 390 (definition of robbery) with penal clauses 392, 393, and 394. Robbery arises when theft or extortion involves causing or attempting death, hurt, or wrongful restraint.

title: Dacoity
old_text: Defined in Section 391 (5 or more persons committing robbery); punished under Section 395 and Section 396 (dacoity with murder).
new_text: Consolidates definition and penalties for dacoity by five or more persons, including capital punishment where murder is committed during dacoity.
punishment_old: Imprisonment for life or RI up to 10 years, and fine; dacoity with murder: death, life, or RI up to 10 years
punishment_new: Imprisonment for life or RI up to 10 years, and fine; dacoity with murder: death or imprisonment for life, and fine
explanation: BNS Section 310 unifies IPC Sections 391, 395, and 396 into a cohesive dacoity provision. Committing robbery jointly by five or more persons constitutes dacoity, and where any member commits murder in commission thereof, every participant is liable to capital punishment or life imprisonment.

title: Robbery or dacoity, with attempt to cause death or grievous hurt
old_text: Using any deadly weapon, or causing grievous hurt, or attempting to cause death or grievous hurt while committing robbery or dacoity.
new_text: Using any deadly weapon or causing grievous hurt or attempting death while committing robbery or dacoity.
punishment_old: Rigorous imprisonment not less than 7 years
punishment_new: Rigorous imprisonment not less than 7 years
explanation: BNS Section 311 corresponds to IPC Section 397 prescribing a non-discretionary mandatory minimum sentence of 7 years rigorous imprisonment. It applies individually to any offender who uses a lethal weapon or inflicts grievous bodily trauma during robbery or dacoity.

title: Attempt to commit robbery or dacoity when armed with deadly weapon
old_text: Attempting to commit robbery or dacoity while armed with any deadly weapon.
new_text: Attempting to commit robbery or dacoity while armed with a deadly weapon.
punishment_old: Rigorous imprisonment not less than 7 years
punishment_new: Rigorous imprisonment not less than 7 years
explanation: BNS Section 312 replaces IPC Section 398 penalizing armed robbery attempts with a mandatory minimum sentence of 7 years rigorous imprisonment. Mere possession and brandishing of deadly arms during an attempt triggers this strict liability.

title: Making preparation to commit dacoity or assembling for purpose of committing dacoity
old_text: Section 399 punished making preparation for dacoity; Section 402 punished assembling of 5 or more persons for dacoity.
new_text: Consolidates preparatory stages of dacoity: making preparations or assembling in a group of five or more for committing dacoity.
punishment_old: Preparation: RI up to 10 years and fine; assembling: RI up to 7 years and fine
punishment_new: Preparation: RI up to 10 years and fine; assembling: RI up to 7 years and fine
explanation: BNS Section 313 merges IPC Section 399 and Section 402, punishing inchoate preparatory actions for dacoity. Unlike ordinary offences where mere preparation is not penal, preparation to commit dacoity attracts up to 10 years rigorous imprisonment.

title: Dishonest misappropriation of property
old_text: Section 403 punished dishonest misappropriation of movable property; Section 404 dealt with property possessed by a deceased person.
new_text: Consolidates dishonest misappropriation or conversion of movable property, with aggravated punishment if property belonged to a deceased person.
punishment_old: General: up to 2 years, or fine, or both; deceased property: up to 3 years (clerk/servant: up to 7 years)
punishment_new: General: up to 2 years, or fine, or both; deceased property: up to 3 years (employee/servant: up to 7 years) and fine
explanation: BNS Section 314 merges IPC Sections 403 and 404 into a unified section. Dishonest conversion of property innocent in origin into one's own use is penalized, with stricter penalties when targeting assets left by deceased individuals.

title: Criminal breach of trust
old_text: Criminal breach of trust defined in Section 405; punishment in Section 406.
new_text: Consolidates definition and general punishment of criminal breach of trust where property entrusted is dishonestly misappropriated.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 3 years, or fine, or both
punishment_new: Imprisonment up to 5 years, or fine, or both
explanation: BNS Section 315 merges IPC Sections 405 and 406. It substantially enhances the maximum term of imprisonment for general criminal breach of trust from 3 years under the IPC to 5 years under the BNS.

title: Criminal breach of trust by carrier, wharfinger, clerk, servant, public servant or banker
old_text: Section 407 (carrier/wharfinger), Section 408 (clerk/servant), and Section 409 (public servant, banker, merchant, factor, broker, attorney, agent).
new_text: Consolidates aggravated categories of criminal breach of trust by carriers, employees, clerks, servants, public servants, bankers, and commercial agents.
punishment_old: Carrier/servant: up to 7 years and fine; public servant/banker: life or up to 10 years and fine
punishment_new: Carrier/employee: up to 7 years and fine; public servant/banker/agent: imprisonment for life or up to 10 years and fine
explanation: BNS Section 316 merges IPC Sections 407, 408, and 409 into a single omnibus provision for aggravated breach of trust. Public servants and bankers face life imprisonment or up to 10 years rigorous imprisonment for misusing entrusted public or client funds.

title: Stolen property, dishonestly receiving or assisting in concealment of stolen property
old_text: Definition in Section 410; Section 411 (receiving), 412 (dacoity stolen property), 413 (habitual receiver), 414 (concealing/assisting).
new_text: Consolidates stolen property definitions, receiving, disposing, concealing, habitual dealing, and handling property obtained by dacoity.
punishment_old: Simple receiving: up to 3 years; dacoity property: life or up to 10 years; habitual: life or up to 10 years
punishment_new: Simple receiving: up to 3 years, or fine, or both; dacoity: life or up to 10 years; habitual receiver: life or up to 10 years and fine
explanation: BNS Section 317 integrates IPC Sections 410 to 414 into an exhaustive stolen property framework. Knowingly receiving stolen property carries up to 3 years imprisonment, rising to life imprisonment for dealing in dacoity plunder or operating as a habitual fence.

title: Cheating
old_text: Cheating defined in Section 415; punished under Section 417 (simple), 418 (cheating with fiduciary knowledge), 420 (cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery).
new_text: Consolidates cheating definitions and sentencing tiers, including cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property (formerly Section 420).
punishment_old: Simple cheating: up to 1 year; cheating with knowledge: up to 3 years; Section 420: up to 7 years and fine
punishment_new: Simple cheating: up to 3 years, or fine, or both; cheating with inducement/delivery of property: up to 7 years and fine
explanation: BNS Section 318 comprehensively consolidates IPC Section 415 (definition), Section 417 (punishment), and the iconic Section 420 (cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property). Offenses historically known under 'IPC 420' are now codified under BNS Section 318(4).

title: Cheating by personation
old_text: Cheating by pretending to be another person, substituting one person for another, or representing oneself as someone else.
new_text: Consolidates definition and enhanced penalty for cheating by personating another real or imaginary person.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 3 years, or fine, or both
punishment_new: Imprisonment up to 5 years, or fine, or both
explanation: BNS Section 319 merges IPC Sections 416 and 419, enhancing the maximum sentence for impersonation fraud from 3 years to 5 years. It covers pretending to be another living or deceased person, or representing a fictitious identity in financial and civil transactions.

title: Dishonest or fraudulent removal or concealment of property to prevent distribution among creditors
old_text: Dishonestly or fraudulently removing, concealing or transferring property without adequate consideration to prevent distribution to creditors.
new_text: Dishonestly or fraudulently removing, concealing, or transferring property to prevent distribution among creditors.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine, or both
punishment_new: Imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine, or both
explanation: BNS Section 320 corresponds to IPC Section 421 penalizing bankruptcy fraud and asset dissipation intended to defeat creditor rights. Fraudulent conveyance of debtor assets attracts up to 2 years imprisonment or fine.

title: Dishonestly or fraudulently preventing debt being made available for creditors
old_text: Dishonestly or fraudulently preventing any debt or demand from being made available according to law for payment of debts.
new_text: Dishonestly preventing any debt or actionable claim from being recovered or applied toward payment of creditors.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine, or both
punishment_new: Imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine, or both
explanation: BNS Section 321 replaces IPC Section 422 penalizing dishonest compromises or sham discharges designed to prevent debts due to an insolvent from reaching legitimate creditors.

title: Dishonest or fraudulent execution of deed of transfer containing false statement of consideration
old_text: Dishonestly signing or executing any deed of transfer containing false statements relating to consideration or beneficiary.
new_text: Executing or becoming party to any deed of transfer containing false recitals regarding consideration or beneficial interest.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine, or both
punishment_new: Imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine, or both
explanation: BNS Section 322 replaces IPC Section 423 penalizing fraudulent transfer deeds containing fabricated consideration amounts or fictitious beneficiaries. It penalizes undervaluation or benami sham recitals intended to defraud creditors or authorities.

title: Dishonest or fraudulent removal or concealment of property
old_text: Dishonestly or fraudulently concealing, removing or assisting in the disposal of property to defraud creditors or courts.
new_text: Dishonestly or fraudulently concealing or removing any property of oneself or another to defraud claimants or prevent execution.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine, or both
punishment_new: Imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine, or both
explanation: BNS Section 323 replaces IPC Section 424 as a general safeguard against clandestine asset stripping and covert property disposal designed to evade civil decrees or creditor claims.

title: Mischief
old_text: Mischief defined in Section 425; general punishment in Section 426 (3 months); damage over Rs. 50 in Section 427 (2 years).
new_text: Consolidates mischief definition with updated monetary loss thresholds: damage over Rs. 20,000 up to 1 year; damage over Rs. 1,00,000 up to 2 years.
punishment_old: Basic: up to 3 months, or fine, or both; damage Rs. 50+: up to 2 years, or fine, or both
punishment_new: Basic: up to 6 months, or fine, or both; damage Rs. 20,000 to Rs. 1,00,000: up to 1 year; damage exceeding Rs. 1,00,000: up to 2 years, or fine, or both
explanation: BNS Section 324 merges IPC Sections 425, 426, and 427 while modernizing archaic damage thresholds. The baseline punishment is increased to 6 months, and modern valuation tiers of Rs. 20,000 and Rs. 1,00,000 replace the colonial 50-rupee clause.

title: Mischief by killing or maiming animal
old_text: Section 428 (killing/maiming animal valued Rs. 10+: up to 2 years); Section 429 (cattle/elephant/horse or value Rs. 50+: up to 5 years).
new_text: Consolidates offences of mischief by killing, poisoning, maiming or rendering useless any animal.
punishment_old: Lesser animal: up to 2 years; cattle/valuable: up to 5 years, or fine, or both
punishment_new: Imprisonment up to 5 years, or fine, or both
explanation: BNS Section 325 merges IPC Sections 428 and 429 into a unified animal protection offence. It eliminates colonial livestock valuation distinctions and prescribes uniform imprisonment extending up to 5 years or fine for killing or maiming any animal.

title: Mischief by injury to public work, bridge, river, road, water supply or navigation
old_text: Covered across Sections 430 (irrigation/water), 431 (public road/bridge), 432 (inundation/drainage), 433 (light/buoy), and 434 (landmarks).
new_text: Consolidates mischief causing damage to public infrastructure, highways, bridges, navigable rivers, flood defenses, water supply, and survey marks.
punishment_old: 5 years to 7 years depending on specific infrastructure clause
punishment_new: Imprisonment up to 5 years, or fine, or both; aggravated public work damage: up to 7 years
explanation: BNS Section 326 merges IPC Sections 430 through 434 into a unified public infrastructure protection provision. Sabotaging canals, roads, bridges, flood embankments, or public utility supplies carries strict imprisonment up to 5 or 7 years.

title: Mischief by fire or explosive substance with intent to cause damage or destroy house, vessel, etc.
old_text: Section 435 (fire to property valued Rs. 100+), 436 (fire to house/worship place), 437 (vessel damage), 438 (fire to vessel).
new_text: Consolidates arson and explosive destruction: damage to property, place of worship, human dwelling, warehouse, or vessel.
punishment_old: General property: up to 7 years; dwelling/worship/vessel: life or up to 10 years, and fine
punishment_new: General property: up to 7 years and fine; dwelling house/place of worship/vessel: imprisonment for life or up to 10 years and fine
explanation: BNS Section 327 integrates IPC Sections 435 through 438 governing arson and explosive sabotage. Arson against human dwellings, places of worship, or ships carries imprisonment for life or up to 10 years rigorous imprisonment.

title: Mischief with intent to destroy or make unsafe rail, aircraft or vessel, or committing mischief having made preparation for hurt
old_text: Section 439 (running vessel ashore with intent to commit theft), Section 440 (mischief committed after preparation for death or hurt).
new_text: Consolidates sabotaging transport vessels, aircraft, or trains to steal cargo or wrecking craft, and mischief committed with preparation for hurt or death.
punishment_old: Section 439: up to 10 years and fine; Section 440: up to 5 years and fine
punishment_new: Imprisonment up to 10 years, and fine
explanation: BNS Section 328 merges IPC Sections 439 and 440. It penalizes hazardous transport sabotage, grounding or stranding vessels/aircraft to loot cargo, and property mischief executed with armed preparation to cause bodily hurt or restraint.

title: Criminal trespass and house-trespass
old_text: Definitions in Sections 441 & 442; punishments in Section 447 (criminal trespass: 3 months) and Section 448 (house-trespass: 1 year).
new_text: Consolidates definitions and baseline punishments for criminal trespass and house-trespass into property in possession of another.
punishment_old: Criminal trespass: up to 3 months, or fine up to Rs. 500, or both; house-trespass: up to 1 year, or fine up to Rs. 1,000, or both
punishment_new: Criminal trespass: up to 3 months, or fine up to Rs. 5,000, or both; house-trespass: up to 1 year, or fine up to Rs. 5,000, or both
explanation: BNS Section 329 merges IPC Sections 441, 442, 447, and 448 into a consolidated baseline trespass provision. Entering property with intent to commit an offence or annoy occupants carries up to 3 months imprisonment, elevated to 1 year for entering human dwellings.

title: Lurking house-trespass and house-breaking
old_text: Defined in Sections 443 (lurking house-trespass) and 445 (house-breaking); punished under Section 453.
new_text: Consolidates definitions and punishment for lurking house-trespass and house-breaking by day.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 2 years, and fine
punishment_new: Imprisonment up to 2 years, and fine
explanation: BNS Section 330 merges IPC Sections 443, 445, and 453. It defines clandestine concealment inside dwellings (lurking house-trespass) and forcible entry through windows, locks, or scaling walls (house-breaking), punishable with up to 2 years imprisonment.

title: House-trespass or house-breaking in order to commit offence or by night
old_text: Spanned 9 individual sections (449 to 458) grading house-trespass and house-breaking by day vs night and gravity of intended crime.
new_text: Consolidates aggravated house-trespass and house-breaking by night, or committed to perpetrate theft, hurt, or offences punishable with death or life imprisonment.
punishment_old: Graded from 2 years up to imprisonment for life depending on night-time, weapons, and offence intended
punishment_new: Graded from 2 years up to imprisonment for life, and fine, depending on intended offence and night commission
explanation: BNS Section 331 consolidates the extensive 9-section complex of IPC Sections 449 through 458 into a single rationalized hierarchy. House-breaking by night or with intent to commit capital crimes attracts the most severe penalties, up to life imprisonment.

title: Grievous hurt or death caused whilst committing lurking house-trespass or house-breaking
old_text: Section 459 (causing grievous hurt/attempting death); Section 460 (joint liability of all persons when death or grievous hurt caused in night house-breaking).
new_text: Consolidates individual and collective liability when death or grievous hurt is caused while committing lurking house-trespass or house-breaking by night.
punishment_old: Imprisonment for life, or imprisonment up to 10 years, and fine
punishment_new: Imprisonment for life, or imprisonment up to 10 years, and fine
explanation: BNS Section 332 merges IPC Sections 459 and 460. Every individual participating in a nighttime house-breaking raid is held jointly liable to life imprisonment or 10 years rigorous imprisonment if any co-intruder causes death or grievous hurt.

title: Dishonestly breaking open receptacle containing property
old_text: Dishonestly or with intent to commit mischief breaking open or unfastening any closed receptacle containing or supposed to contain property.
new_text: Dishonestly breaking open, unfastening or unlocking any safe, chest or closed receptacle containing or believed to contain property.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine, or both
punishment_new: Imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine, or both
explanation: BNS Section 333 replaces IPC Section 461 penalizing opening locked safes, trunks, or security boxes without authorization. Forcibly tampering with closed storage containers carries imprisonment up to 2 years or fine.

title: Punishment for same offence when committed by person entrusted with custody
old_text: Breaking open closed receptacle by a person entrusted with custody of the closed receptacle.
new_text: Breaking open or unfastening closed receptacle containing property by a person specifically entrusted with its custody.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 3 years, or fine, or both
punishment_new: Imprisonment up to 3 years, or fine, or both
explanation: BNS Section 334 replaces IPC Section 462 punishing custodians, guards, or bank locker attendants who break open sealed containers entrusted to their charge. The breach of trusted custody incurs up to 3 years imprisonment.
